At this stage, use your childlike superpowers to come into the "Wow of Now" (have you seen the movie Waking Life?), and make sure there's enough safety around you to continue with reparenting. 2. This can almost feel like playing house as a kid where you imagined how you'd take care of a baby, etc. 3. Practice being the adult -- do at least one part of caring for yourself while support is still there from the previous step. 4. Adult mode itself -- after sufficient practice with reparenting, you become a natural at sending love to little you, protecting them, and shepherding them. 5. Adult and child in relationship -- the adult leads. The child isn't pushed away, but doesn't have to run the whole life alone. This can actually feel really weird if you've been stuck in forced adulthood for a while. Our goal is to go from weird to silly and playful. Lose self-consciousness while gaining self-awareness, if that makes sense!

article: I think this is closer to Buddhist practice too. The point is not an impossible performance in which nothing unskillful ever appears. In one discourse (sutta), AN 6.63, the Buddha defines karma in terms of intention (so if you didn't mean to cause harm, your mind is not poisoned). In DN 2, he explains that in the training to purify the mind, one first recognizes a fault, makes amends, and then restrains themself to prevent that kind of thing in future. So it's not like, "you're either pure, or you're not," which is where a lot of folks stay stuck. If you're ashamed about some pattern you have, that might be a signal to give some attention to how you can improve on that pattern. If it's shame just because of an intrusive thought, then it's probably not adaptive, and can be simply let go of.

Other types of manipulation to check for include: Gaslighting, when your perception of reality is slowly giving way to someone else's. Combat this by trusting your perceptions (after documenting or double checking).

In abusive relationships, gaslighting often turns into D.A.R.V.O.: Deny, Attack, and Reverse Victim and Offender. This is how the abuser flips the script on accountability. If you notice this happening, extricate yourself quickly.
